title: Redwood discovery - Kestrel Fintech - latency & throughput
summary: Intro discovery focused on latency and throughput requirements for Kestrel's customer-facing fraud scoring and conversational assistant. Kestrel needs p95 <= 350ms for short prompts at 4-8k concurrency budget, streaming for progressive responses, and clear guidance on cost tradeoffs between Hosted and Dedicated/Private deployments. Action items: bench plan, pricing for Dedicated tiers, security docs, and a follow-up benchmark run with a 1k token workload.
transcript:
Header: 2026-03-22 16:00 UTC | Duration: ~47m | Redwood: Alex, Priya, Jordan | Kestrel: Michael, Sarah, Tom, Rita

00:00 Alex (Redwood): hey everyone thanks for joining, i'm alex chen from redwood, i'm the AE on this account. priya and jordan from our se team are with me. quick round robin?
00:12 Michael (Kestrel): michael here, cto, we run Kestrel's infra. Sarah lead ml, Tom infra, Rita security. thanks for making time.
00:22 Priya (Redwood SE): thanks. goal today is to understand p95 targets, concurrency and whether hosted meets them or you need dedicated/private. we'll talk streaming, batching, kv cache.
00:34 Sarah: high level, two prod use cases: 1) fraud chat assistant — short prompts 30-200 tokens, strict latency p95 target ~300ms; 2) contextual reports — long prompts up to 1k tokens, throughput matters more.
00:50 Tom: we expect bursts up to 4k concurrent requests with typical steady of 800-1,200. want ability to autoscale quickly.
01:03 Alex: cool, that's helpful. hosted api can hit low latencies for smaller models, but for your p95 300ms at 4k concurrency we may recommend Dedicated reserved capacity or Private with pinned GPUs. want to dig into model size and token/sec expectations.
01:20 Sarah: models aren't finalized. we're experimenting with a 7B and a distilled 13B. quality bar requires at least 13B for assistant but we can try 7B for fraud scoring if latency gains are worth it.
01:34 Priya: good to know. two axes: model selection and infra. On hosted we provide autoscaling across pools which is great for bursts but multi-tenant variability sometimes adds tail. Dedicated gives you single-tenant GPU pools with predictable p95. Private gives you network control/KMS for compliance.
01:50 Michael: what's the delta in p95 and cost roughly between hosted and dedicated?
01:57 Priya: approximate numbers: for a 13B model, hosted p95 for a short 100-token prompt might be 250-450ms depending on region and load; Dedicated with reserved GPUs and optimized kernels usually brings that down 10-30% and tightens the tail. cost-wise Dedicated is higher fixed commit but lower per-token at scale. we'll send a pricing tier.
02:19 Tom: streaming — we need progressive tokens to UI as they generate, can't wait for full decode. any gotchas?
02:25 Jordan: streaming supported across modes; on Dedicated/Private you can get lower first-byte latency by tuning batching and smaller micro-batches. streaming does increase connection management but we support chunked streaming and function-like tool-calls.
02:39 Sarah: want p95 first-byte under 150ms ideally for short prompts. is that realistic?
02:45 Priya: for sub-150ms first-byte you probably need a small model and aggressive micro-batching or dedicated GPUs on a low-latency region. also prefix/KV cache can shave token generation time if many requests share context.
03:03 Michael: can you run token/sec bench for the 13B quantized model? our current internal perf team gets ~60 tokens/sec on their infra per GPU but with high variance.
03:14 Priya: we can run a benchmark; typical optimized kernels on our runtime hit 80-120 token/sec on A10/A100-ish hardware for 13B depending on quantization and sequence length; for 7B you might see 200-400 tokens/sec. we'll propose a 1k-token and 100-token bench plan.
03:33 Sarah: concurrency math: if we need 4k concurrent with 100-token average and target 300ms p95, that feels impossible without batching? how do you recommend sizing?
03:45 Priya: right, throughput and latency tradeoff. If you need <300ms for p95 at 4k concurrent short prompts, Dedicated with many serving replicas and small micro-batches helps; also edge routing and regional placement. Another lever is autoscaling policies with burst capacity. We'll provide sample capacity maps.
04:05 Tom: on VPC/private, how tight is the control on network egress and kms? we have strict compliance.
04:12 Alex: Private deployments give you a customer-managed control plane, VPC peering and HSM/KMS integration. we can provide SOC2 docs and a VPC network diagram. Rita, will that meet your audit needs?
04:24 Rita (Kestrel Security): probably, need to review encryption at rest, key rotation, audit logs retention. also SSO/SAML and RBAC.
04:32 Marta (Redwood CSM): we have an enterprise pack doc with retention options and SOC2/ISO references, we'll share after.
04:39 Michael: what about KV cache/prefix cache — we have a lot of repeated user context for fraud signals. can that cut latency?
04:46 Priya: yes, prefix caching reduces the KV-cache warmup. If multiple requests share a common prefix (like user profile or common system prompt), you can cache KV states and skip the recompute. This helps p95, especially for longer sequences. We'll recommend cache hit rate targets.
05:02 Sarah: any gotchas with quantization for quality? we can't lose false positive detection sensitivity.
05:09 Jordan: quantization is model and workload dependent. for some 13B variants a 4-bit quantization preserves quality well; for others you might see regressions. we recommend eval harness runs tied to your prompt set and guardrail regression alerts.
05:26 Michael: what about fallbacks — if Dedicated saturated, automatic fallback to hosted?
05:31 Priya: yes, smart routing policies can fallback to compatible model variants hosted or in other regions. there's a cost/latency trade but it keeps service online.
05:42 Tom: what logs and tracing do we get for per-request latency breakdown?
05:46 Alex: Console gives token-level cost and latency breakdown, per-route dashboards, and traces. We can stream logs to your SIEM and provide sampling.
05:56 Sarah: timeline: we want a POC in 6 weeks, with bench in 2 weeks. Is that realistic?
06:03 Alex: yes, we can do a bench in 10 business days if we get sample prompts and dataset; POC in 6 weeks is typical.
06:10 Michael: ok let's talk bench specifics: we will provide 500 representative short prompts and 100 long prompts (1k tokens). we need you to run streaming and non-streaming tests, and provide p50/p95/p99 numbers and tokens/sec, and CPU/GPU util.
06:26 Priya: perfect. we'll propose test matrix: 100-token, 1k-token; concurrency sweep 100/500/1k/4k; streaming and batch; models 7B distill and 13B quantized and fp16. We'll include per-token latency breakdown.
06:44 Sarah: how do you measure p95? from client perspective or server side? slight variance matters.
06:50 Jordan: we emit both client-perceived and server-side metrics. Client side includes network and TLS, server side is internal decode latency; both provided.
07:01 Michael: cost models — provide per-token and per-hour for Dedicated reserved tiers plus host fallback pricing?
07:07 Alex: yes we'll send pricing options. Expect a commit for Dedicated (monthly) with lower per-token for high throughput; Hosted is pay-as-you-go but higher per-token at scale. We'll include burst pricing and burst-capacity options.
07:20 Tom: autoscaling and cold start — do you have cold-start issues with KV caches?
07:26 Priya: cold starts can affect KV cache warmup for new model instances; we mitigate with pre-warming and cache warmup scripts. Dedicated helps since you control pool sizes.
07:39 Rita: security follow-up: want SOC2 report, KMS integration doc, and SAML SSO setup.
07:45 Marta: we'll attach enterprise security docs and schedule a security review workshop with our compliance team.
07:51 Michael: SLA and incident response — what's your standard?
07:55 Alex: Dedicated comes with an SLA and priority support; hosted has standard uptime SLA. We'll send SLA matrix.
08:03 Sarah: ok can we get a sample run with 1k token to see token/sec and memory usage?
08:08 Priya: yes, that's part of the bench. We'll propose hardware: A100-80GB or H100 for 13B fp16; A10/A100 for some quantized runs.
08:20 Michael: curious on warmup for prefix cache — do you store per-customer caches and how much memory?
08:26 Jordan: caches are per-tenant configurable with eviction policies. Memory depends on KV size, we'll provide estimates. For many customers prefix caches for 1k-token context can be tens of GB at scale.
08:40 Sarah: any public benchmarks you can share?
08:43 Alex: we have internal perf dashboards and a public model catalog with verified profiles; we'll share redwood model perf sheet and previous bench artifacts.
08:52 Tom: if we go private on-prem, what's the onboarding time?
08:56 Priya: private on-prem typical 8-12 weeks depending on network and hardware procurement. VPC/private cloud faster, 3-6 weeks.
09:06 Michael: long list of asks, what's the immediate next step?
09:09 Alex: we'll send: 1) bench plan and template for sample prompts, 2) Dedicated pricing tiers and commit options, 3) security pack (SOC2, KMS, SSO doc), 4) proposed dates for bench run and follow-up deep dive.
09:23 Sarah: can you include a proposed capacity map and cost estimation for our 4k concurrency peak?
09:29 Alex: yes, we'll include capacity map with baseline and peak scenarios.
09:34 Rita: please set expectations on quality regressions with quantization and provide evaluation criteria.
09:39 Jordan: will include regression alert thresholds and sample eval harness config.
09:45 Michael: ok let's wrap. appreciate the clarity.
09:49 Alex: recap and next steps: (1) redwood to receive prompt sets by Mar 24; (2) bench run scheduled week of Mar 30; (3) security docs shared by Mar 24; (4) pricing + capacity map by Mar 25.
09:59 Sarah: sounds good. thanks everyone.
10:03 End of transcript.

Notes: transcript has occasional misattribution and minor transcription errors (speaker labels approximate).
